questions.q: Which e-mail protocol keeps messages on the server so that the same mailbox stays in sync across a phone, tablet and laptop?
questions.solution: IMAP stores mail on the server and synchronises state across devices. POP3 traditionally downloads and removes mail (single-device model), SMTP sends, FTP moves files.

questions.q: Mail merge in MS Word is used to:
options: Merge two documents into one file
Create personalised copies of a document for many recipients
questions.solution: Mail merge generates letters/labels/envelopes/e-mails where a common main document is personalised from a data source - one template, many recipients.
questions.shortcut: 'Same letter, many names' = mail merge; the trap options play on the word 'merge'.

questions.q: At which layer of the OSI model does a switch primarily operate?
questions.solution: Switches forward frames using MAC (hardware) addresses, which belong to the Data Link layer (2). Routers use IP at layer 3.
questions.shortcut: MAC-address device = layer 2; IP device = layer 3.

questions.q: Which shortcut sets double line spacing in MS Word?
questions.solution: Ctrl+2 gives double spacing, Ctrl+1 single spacing and Ctrl+5 1.5 spacing. Ctrl+D opens the Font dialog.
questions.shortcut: The digit is the spacing; 5 means 1.5.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The quality of the mangoes sold in these markets ___ improved this year.
questions.solution: The head noun is *quality* (singular); *of the mangoes sold in these markets* is only a descriptive phrase. A singular subject with present perfect needs **has improved**.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

My sister **prefers coffee than** tea in winter.
questions.solution: **Prefer X to Y**: prefers coffee **to** tea. The original's subject is third person singular, so *prefers* with the -s must stay — only the partner word changes.
questions.shortcut: prefer → to; keep the subject-verb agreement.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

By the time the firefighters arrived, the wooden shed ___ to ashes.
questions.solution: 'By the time + past event' makes the blank the earlier of two past actions → past perfect: **had burnt**. Present-perfect options clash with the past anchor, and 'was burning' describes a mid-process rather than the completed ruin.
questions.shortcut: By-the-time ladder: earlier event → had + participle.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: The contrast is 'decoration rather than ___', and the passage argues trees are functional city assets — cooling, dust-trapping, noise-softening. The noun for functional city assets is **infrastructure**. *Entertainment, souvenir, ceremony* fit the grammar but belong to no part of the argument.
questions.shortcut: Contrast frame 'X rather than Y' wants Y from the same serious category as the argument — trees as urban equipment.
questions.passage: Concrete has conquered our cities, and the first casualty has been the tree. A mature tree on a street does more than look (1) ______: it drops the temperature of its surroundings, traps dust and softens the noise of traffic. Yet when roads are widened, it is usually the tree that (2) ______ way. Municipal budgets treat planting as decoration rather than (3) ______, so saplings are planted in a rush before elections and forgotten soon afterwards. Survival, not planting, is the real (4) ______; a sapling needs watering for three full summers before it can stand on its own. Cities that have understood this simple point now pay residents a small sum to (5) ______ the trees outside their homes — and their streets are visibly greener.

questions.q: With reference to NITI Aayog, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: It was set up in 2014 as the successor to the Finance Commission
It is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament
It continues the Five Year Plan process
It was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission
questions.solution: NITI Aayog was created by a **Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015**, replacing the Planning Commission (1950) after the 12th Plan ended. It is neither constitutional nor statutory, and it does not allocate Plan funds.
questions.shortcut: Statutory test fails → only the '1 Jan 2015 replacement' statement can be true.

questions.q: Who renounced his knighthood in protest against the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** of 1919?
questions.solution: **Rabindranath Tagore** gave up the knighthood conferred on him in 1915 by writing to the Viceroy (Lord Chelmsford) in May 1919. Gandhi later returned his Kaiser-i-Hind medal.
questions.shortcut: Only a 'Sir' could renounce a knighthood → Sir Rabindranath.

questions.q: The Income-tax Act, 2025, which becomes effective from 1 April 2026, is notable for:
options: introducing a single 'tax year' and replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961
raising the basic exemption limit to ₹7 lakh
questions.solution: The Income-tax Act, 2025 consolidates the 1961 Act into **536 sections across 23 chapters** and replaces the previous-year/assessment-year pair with one **'tax year'** (first applicable to income of FY 2026-27). Rates and slabs are essentially unchanged; GST law is untouched.
questions.shortcut: Keyword of the new Act = 'tax year' — nothing about GST or new slabs.

questions.q: Which committee recommended a two-tier Panchayati Raj system consisting of Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat?
questions.solution: The **Ashok Mehta Committee (1977)** suggested a **two-tier** scheme — Zila Parishad at the district and Mandal Panchayat (cluster of villages) below it. Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) had recommended **three tiers**, G.V.K. Rao (1985) wanted the district as the planning unit, and L.M. Singhvi (1986) sought constitutional status.
questions.shortcut: Tier count mnemonic: Balwant-3, Ashok-2 ('B-A = 3-2'), Rao-district, Singhvi-Constitution.

questions.q: A train 120 m long is running at 54 km/h. The time it takes to pass a signal post is:
A bus travels 240 km at a uniform speed of 60 km/h. The journey takes:
The average age of a husband and wife at the time of their marriage was 23 years. After 5 years they have a one-year-old child. The average age of the family of three now is:
questions.solution:
Marriage total = 2 × 23 = 46. After 5 years: 46 + 5 + 5 = 56.
Child adds 1 year: total = 57.
Average $= \frac{57}{3} = 19$ years.
questions.shortcut: Both adults age 5 (total 56), child is 1 ⇒ 57/3 = 19. (Trap: forgetting to add the child's own age.)

questions.q: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 10. The number exceeds the number obtained by reversing its digits by 36. Find the number.
questions.solution:
Let the number be $10a + b$ with $a + b = 10$.
$(10a + b) - (10b + a) = 9(a - b) = 36 \Rightarrow a - b = 4$.
$a = 7, b = 3$ → number $= 73$.
questions.shortcut: Only 73 and 37 have digit sum 10 with gap 4; the number is bigger than its reverse, so 73.

questions.q:
**Statements:** A few students are athletes. All athletes are fit.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some students are fit.
II. All students are athletes.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
questions.solution: 'A few' = plain Some: the student-athlete is fit → I follows. II is the reverse-All trap. **Only I.**
questions.shortcut: No guaranteed outside part with 'a few' — do not import only-a-few rules.

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**38   27   11**

**54   18   9**

**46   37   ?**
questions.solution: Adding digit sums separately fails (11 + 9 = 20 ≠ 11). Add first, then sum the digits: 38 + 27 = 65 → 11 ✓; 54 + 18 = 72 → 9 ✓. So 46 + 37 = 83 → 8 + 3 = **11**. (20 is the separate digit-sum trap.)
questions.shortcut: Carries make S(a+b) differ from S(a)+S(b) — test both.

questions.q: In a certain code, **BAT is coded 23** (sum of alphabet positions). How is **CUP** coded?
Select the related number: **4 : 20 :: 6 : 42 :: 8 : ?**
questions.shortcut: Two model pairs pin the rule exactly — with n(n+1) confirmed, no other reading competes.
